newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 21.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 21.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Tuesday:

* Indonesia central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono said the bank would continue to implement and adjust market friendly instrument, such as open market operations, discount windows and the reserve requirement, to control money supply.

* On Monday, the Dow Jones Industrial average ended up 67.73 points at 6,843.87 mostly on upbeat earnings from high-technology companies, but the market was nervous ahead of testimony Tuesday by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan on the economy.
* Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana said on Saturday the government will not raise domestic fuel oil prices, at least until the end of 1997.
MARKETS
* On Monday, the Jakarta composite index closed up 10.16 points on the day, or 1.53 percent, at 674.13 points following sustained active buying of heavyweights and medium-caps.
* On Tuesday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,370.30/70.60 in early trading against the opening of 2,370.00/71.50.
STOCKS TO WATCH
* Astra International on announcement that it would hold an extraordinary general meeting on February 19 to discuss changes in the board of commissioners
* Astra Graphia on announcement that the firm had agreed to merge with footwear company PT Mitracorp Footwear International from January 1, 1997.
* State-controlled telecommunications firms Indosat and Telkom on news report that both company officials denied rumours of their possible merger.

* Toll road builder and operator Citra Marga on reports that the company posted a net profit of 123.6 bln rph in 1996. On Monday, Standard & Poor said it had assigned a BBB-minus rating to the proposed US$100 million 144A notes issue by Citra Marga Finance BV, which is guaranteed by PT Citra Marga Nusaphala Persada.
* Cahaya Kalbar on news that it posted a net profit of 17 billion rupiah in 1996, against 6.6 billion in 1995.
*Bank Bira on news it posted a net profit of 60 billion rupiah in 1996, up from 30.34 billion in 1995.

* Ciputra Development on news it expected a net profit of 130.6 billion rupiah in 1996, against 93.1 billion in 1995. It also planned to start a 200 billion rupiah housing project in East Java later this year.
* Pharmaceutical firm Kalbe Farma on news it planned to acquire the assets of two Australian firms worth around $14.75 million.
* Distribution firm Enseval on market talk of a possible link-up with a foreign partner.
* Bank BNI on news it plans to issue $145 million Yankee bonds through its New York office
* Hero Supermarket on market talk of possible target of acquisition of the Lippo Group.
